p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Ethosuximide, an approved antiseizure drug; the class contrast is T-type calcium-channel block. Formulation not carried; no dose, route or schedule.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Origin: the Wwox-null mouse PTZ experiment (WWOX-direct), not another disease. Transfer to human WOREE: untested; one experiment, one laboratory, symptomatic class at best.
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Not found in the research (dated queries 2026-10-21, R2 note section 13): no abstract-indexed paper for WWOX with ethosuximide, and one hit for WWOX with T-type terms that holds gene counts only. By dismissal-ledger D-37 this licenses 'no abstract-indexed paper', not 'never measured': the one Wwox ethosuximide assay sits inside a paper whose abstract lacks the term.
p4_roadmap_fields.known_roads_state: Partial (known-roads note 2.3), now narrowed by the R2 note: not a clean genotype-specific effect. The lithium arm of the same figure suppressed in all three genotypes (relevant negative on specificity).
p4_roadmap_fields.path_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (symptomatic class). The lead would become a mechanism to test only if the falsifier survives; it is not a RECUPERO_PROFONDO candidate.
p4_roadmap_fields.expected_contribution: Symptom (provoked seizure). Not disease modification: in a digenic absence mouse (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE) the ethosuximide effect and a Cav3.1 deletion suppressed the seizure and left a quantified comorbidity untouched (R2 section 6).
p4_roadmap_fields.mechanism: Premise: T-type block pulls back an excess created by loss of WWOX. UNKNOWN in WWOX. Non-T-type routes reported for ethosuximide in non-WWOX systems: GIRK block, a reticular-nucleus site, broad cortical effects, a FOXO-pathway effect in worms; none shown in a Wwox system. T-type excess is a recognised cause of disease in humans (gain-of-function variants in the T-type channel genes) but is not shown in a WWOX null. Candidate extra read-out proposed by R2: phospho-Ser9 GSK3 beta in any Wwox-null ethosuximide experiment (an IPOTESI from two non-matching systems). Figure read (IT12 P2.2, 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): in Xenopus oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by wild-type Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.055 millimolar, BELOW the shaded therapeutic band (about 0.25 to 0.9 millimolar), and the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus wild-type Gbeta-gamma channel at about 1.2 millimolar, ABOVE the band (partial block, about 25 to 45 percent across it, our calculation from the printed Hill fit); the paper's text gives about 1.5 to 2 and about 1 millimolar for that channel, and the about 0.55 millimolar value of the supplementary fit table belongs to the K78R patient variant, which an earlier version of this sentence had merged with the wild type (corrected 2026-11-25, ADV-279); the authors state that neuronal abundance of the homomer is unknown. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; no Wwox-system GIRK change is measured.
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: Internal, WWOX: DL-MECH-170, CLAIM 016 and its lithium boundary note, Cheng 2020 manifest, FT-115. R2 note (scientist-b), landed on main (integration commit 190b389e; closure commit 743f9914 records three blind audits, among them the Cheng 2020 locators 6 of 6 SUPPORTED with soft corrections, and wording repairs that are themselves unaudited); its narrowing of DL-MECH-170 remains owed a blind audit by someone else. Adjacent, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: the R2 papers (Gnb1, Gabrb3, Hcn1, Cntnap2, Grin2b, digenic absence, worm and relay-neuron strain studies).
p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Pro: in one three-genotype experiment ethosuximide's effect was marked significant in the null panel only. Contra: late-phase restriction; cohort variability of a comparable order to the effect; the wild-type baseline is small but not zero, and lithium was still detected inside the same low range (so a pure floor effect is not established); no interaction test; Gnb1 mouse shows the default outcome of a mutant-only effect when the wild-type baseline is near zero; mechanism may be non-T-type; a measured non-T-type target at labelled exposure exists in oocytes (GIRK, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B), and in a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6); GAERS has less T-type current than its control.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Not assessed in any record read. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing. FT-115 (no patient-level T-type evidence) was confirmed at full-text depth for four documents (R2 section 13) and is not retired as a statement about the literature.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN. No human age-at-treatment datum of any kind exists; no experiment in any WWOX model varies age at treatment beyond mouse P5 (early-benefit note, section 4).
p4_roadmap_fields.pharmacology: UNKNOWN for a Wwox system. The R2 note carries, from papers it read, that ethosuximide's own T-type potency is in the millimolar range and disputed at relevant concentrations; exposure and CNS exposure in WOREE: UNKNOWN. Its reported GIRK potency in oocytes, against the figure band (about 0.25 to 0.9 millimolar), is below the band for the GIRK2 homomer and above it for the wild-type GIRK1/2 channel, which would still be partly blocked inside it (corrected 2026-11-25, ADV-279), so the potency argument does not by itself say that T-type block is the operative route. Class-level exposure and potency facts, no dose, no score, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE [IT59 2026-11-20 unit B packet change]: in male Swiss mice of 24 to 30 grams (no age given), total brain ethosuximide was 134.9 micrograms per gram of wet tissue (about 0.96 millimolar as total tissue, not a free concentration; the brain was homogenised 1 to 2 in water and no dilution correction is stated) at the time scheduled for a seizure test, 45 minutes after an intraperitoneal dose that was about half the dose of the one Wwox experiment (arithmetic; the value is the saline co-treated arm of a mouse interaction study of another question, PMID 22315091); in the mouse, serum and brain concentrations equilibrate within minutes and the half-life is about one hour (an old abstract-level report). Potency at T-type channels is reported inconsistently in the sources read, by different assays that are not comparable: about six-tenths of a millimolar in a ChEMBL row without a mapped gene (SCI's reading of the primary paper reports a persistent current in recombinant human channels) against above five millimolar in one FLIPR assay at one channel subtype (one ChEMBL transcription). PUP EXPOSURE IS UNKNOWN: no juvenile exposure of any kind was found by the routes read, and the age of the one Wwox drug experiment is not stated; the first measurement an exposure-controlled test needs is the brain exposure at the regimen of that experiment. Label (openFDA record, newest 2026-05-25): indicated for absence seizures; safety and effectiveness below the age of three years not established. Added class-level facts from the T-type sheet and the held full texts, no dose, no score, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE, no ranking of the agents [IT59 2026-11-20 fourth packet change]: WITHIN ONE DOCUMENT (Epilepsia Open 2026, adult Gabrb3 D120N knock-in mice, atypical-absence video-EEG, a within-subjects crossover; the full text was read by SCI and the abstract by HE) ethosuximide and ulixacaltamide each reduced seizure incidence against its own vehicle; the authors' printed Results give a 64 percent reduction for both, from separate comparisons against vehicle, with different vehicle means and unequal group sizes, so the two figures are NOT a direct contrast (the abstract gives no percentage, no ethosuximide-against-ulixacaltamide test is reported, and the paper measures no exposure). In adult rats kindled in the amygdala (Casillas-Espinosa 2015, open full text) ulixacaltamide at four doses, ethosuximide and carbamazepine were given to the same rats in a randomised crossover (abstract); ulixacaltamide was not effective at suppressing seizures in fully kindled rats (HE read the full text; ethosuximide's own result in that document is SCI's reading) while it delayed the progression of kindling, which the authors describe as no anti-seizure effect in that model. HARM, class level and animal only: in the same document ulixacaltamide produced slight sedation and slow movement at the third of its four doses in fully kindled rats, not statistically different from vehicle, and mild adverse effects (a score of 1) in the first week of kindling progression, a different arm (HE read the full text); at the top dose the animals were sedate with reduced movement and a higher score (the paper's words; 'marked' is SCI's word, which HE did not re-read); a 2018 abstract reports subtle impairment of a touchscreen learning task at the highest of three doses. A class hypothesis, not a finding about ethosuximide: the T-type blocker TTA-A2 acutely increased sleep, lowered core body temperature and prevented diet-induced weight gain in normal-weight animals and reduced body weight and fat mass in obese rodents (a 2009 abstract), so a weight or temperature effect in a small pup is a reading to make before any comparison. ORDERING: the potency rows of ulixacaltamide (the same three numbers in three records) and of apinocaltamide (one document) are one origin each, and TTA-A2 has its binding and Cav3.2 values quoted again; no document tests two of the three selective agents; they sit at single digits to tens of nanomolar in cell assays, against sub-millimolar to millimolar or above for ethosuximide in different assays and laboratories (the one within-document pair is TTA-P2 against ethosuximide in one plate assay at one channel subtype, a difference of orders of magnitude on potency only); no brain concentration of any selective agent was found by these routes, and the adult mouse total brain value above is the only measured brain figure in the class found by these routes; potency, state dependence and exposure therefore do not order the agents.
p4_roadmap_fields.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. Class-level signal only: T-type blockers reduce progenitor viability in vitro (research compounds, rat, Cav3.1-dependent), significance unknown. In a DEE mouse model (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE) some antiseizure drug classes aggravated spiking, so 'an antiseizure drug suppresses in the mutant' is not a safe default and a falsifier needs a harm arm. Suitability not presumed.
p4_roadmap_fields.verification_scope: Supported by: one experiment (Cheng 2020). R2 re-read depth: partial. The R2 note has landed and three of its readings were blind-audited at its closure; the narrowing of the lead and of the CLAIM 016 framing, and the wording repairs, are unaudited: blind audit OWED. This card was blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (the sections this version repairs are unaudited).
p4_roadmap_fields.question_history: DL-MECH-170 (open), CLAIM 016, FT-115, known-roads note 2.3, R2 note.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: Is the late-phase ethosuximide effect in the null reproduced, with a drug-by-genotype interaction test, a concurrent same-day PTZ-alone control in every cell and a per-genotype baseline stated? Read it on the proportional scale or as a wild-type simple effect; the 2026-11-15 figure extraction does not bound the size. The R2 design sketch says power depends mainly on which control cohort is representative, not on N alone.
p4_roadmap_fields.status: IPOTESI (open lead; the R2 note has landed, its narrowing and wording repairs are unaudited).
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Replaces 'the drug the paper did not favour behaved genotype-specifically' with the time-resolved reading, the cohort-variability problem, the non-T-type mechanisms and a class-level developmental safety line.

evaluation_frame.source: repurposing_10h_scientist-d_20261021.md, 'The answer in one page', DESIGN TABLE A and B. INFERENZA built from precedents that are all NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; the manifests of that note were blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (207 of 215 triples supported, eight repaired; the repairs are unaudited).
a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); no measurement of the scatter of an untreated interval in WOREE is established here (the repository's series have one timepoint per patient; no wider search was run)
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter

the word protection: in the human precedents read for this frame none measured the preservation of a function that would otherwise have been lost; the repository's mouse rescue studies are outside this frame and the scope of 'this corpus' is not defined, so no wider negative is established here

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.
